Revised assessment with literature context

Score: -0.40

Key sentence: "The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook."

Why the score changed (finance/econ literature insights):
- Zero lower bound and deflation risk: Market-based inflation compensation declined while the policy rate moved to the effective lower bound (0–0.25%). Literature associates such conditions with liquidity trap dynamics and downside risks to activity when inflation expectations soften and policy space narrows, absent forceful non-rate tools (monetary policy and liquidity buffers references on liquidity trap and deflation risk).
- Credit channel mitigation: The Fed’s large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount window easing, and dollar swap lines should compress external finance premia and support balance sheets, moderating the downturn (credit view; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994; Gertler and Gilchrist 1994; Oliner and Rudebusch 1996a).
- Balance sheet stress amplifiers: Weak business fixed investment and stress in the energy sector imply worsening firm balance sheets and higher agency costs, which can deepen recessions without policy support (bank capital, credit market imperfections, and agency cost references).
- Expectations and credibility: Survey-based longer-term inflation expectations were little changed; anchoring expectations is consistent with best practices in inflation-targeting frameworks and helps stabilize real activity when conventional policy is constrained (Svensson on inflation forecast targeting; central bank objectives and credibility references).

Overall tone remains negative due to the severe near-term shock and deflationary pressures, but is less negative than -0.55 because the announced QE, liquidity facilities, and swap lines are expected—per the credit channel literature—to mitigate the contraction and support financial intermediation.
